predecessors.name: Grand Duchy of Baden
predecessors.text: the Grand Duchy of Baden, whose Grand Duke fled Karlsruhe on the night of 13/14 May 1849

successors.name: Grand Duchy of Baden
successors.text: the grand duchy, restored when Rastatt surrendered on 23 July 1849

ledger.x: 13/14 May 1849: the Rastatt garrison has mutinied (9 May) and Grand Duke Leopold flees Karlsruhe, so Baden passes to the revolutionaries.
May 1849: the revolutionaries take the grand duchy; on 1 June 'Under Lorenz Brentano a provisional democratic government is formed'.

June 1849: Prussian, federal and Hessian troops invade Baden 'in order to defeat the revolution'; Hirschfeld wins at Waghausel on 21/22 June and a dictatorial government under Goegg and Werner forms on 28 June.
23 July 1849: the revolutionary government ends with the fall of Rastatt; the grand duchy passes back to its grand duke.

wars.name: Baden Revolution
wars.outcome: The Prussian-led invasion beat the revolutionaries at Waghausel (21/22 June), entered Freiburg (7 July) and took Rastatt (23 July 1849), ending the revolution.

certainty.note: The revolutionaries held the grand duchy within its existing frontiers; no page opened states those frontiers' survey, so this is an inherited-frontier reading.
